title: How Does Blockchain Work?
target_audience: General audience interested in technology and financial innovations
learning_objectives: Understand the basic structure and components of a blockchain
Identify the role of blocks and chains in ensuring data integrity
Grasp the concept of decentralization and its importance

scenes.title: Introduction to Blockchain
scenes.narration: Imagine a digital ledger, recording every transaction made and shared with everyone. That's the essence of blockchain. But how does it actually work?
scenes.visual_description: Animation of a digital notebook being passed around a circle of people, illustrating the concept of shared ledgers.

scenes.title: The Anatomy of a Block
scenes.narration: Each 'block' in a blockchain contains three basic elements: data, a unique hash, and the hash of the previous block. Think of it like a train—each carriage holds cargo (data), its own identifier (hash), and a latch to the previous carriage (previous hash).
scenes.visual_description: Show a train with labeled carriages, each containing cargo (data) and labeled with unique IDs (hashes). Connections between carriages show previous hashes.

scenes.title: Chains and Security
scenes.narration: These blocks link together to form a chain. The beauty here is in security—if someone tries to alter a block's data, its hash changes, breaking the chain. The network spots this and rejects the altered block. Imagine trying to sneak an extra carriage into the train—immediately noticeable!
scenes.visual_description: Visual of breaking a chain when one block is tampered with, followed by a red alert symbolizing rejection.

scenes.title: Decentralization: The Core
scenes.narration: Instead of a single entity controlling the ledger, it's decentralized, meaning power is distributed among all participants. It reduces the risk of fraud and failure. Imagine everyone owning a copy of the train's schedule—unity in transparency.
scenes.visual_description: Participants holding identical copies of a document, representing decentralization.
